# Architecture

How MNML is put together: a Home Assistant integration that serves the cards, their editors and their templates and installs the theme, all built from this repository and released as one `mnml.zip`. For how the cards behave, see [How the cards work](cards.md); for how they look, [Design](design.md); for the theme, [The theme](theme.md).

## The parts

| Path                      | What                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/contract/`           | The contract (`cards.ts`, `entities.ts`, `templates.ts`) and what the cards and their users both read                                                                     |
| `src/cards/`              | The cards, their base class, the known-key schemas, the registration and the loader; `parts/` holds what several cards share                                              |
| `src/ha/`                 | Home Assistant in the browser: the typed `hass`, formatting, names, rules, conditions, navigation, motion, and the template parts that draw Home Assistant's own elements |
| `src/store/`              | The integration's template store in the browser, and the shipped families fetched on demand                                                                               |
| `src/editors/`            | The card editors and their description vocabulary                                                                                                                         |
| `src/panel/`              | The MNML panel                                                                                                                                                            |
| `src/templates/`          | The template engine, discovery, the shipped templates' loader, the dashboard expander                                                                                     |
| `templates/`              | The shipped templates, one YAML file per family                                                                                                                           |
| `src/home/`               | The home generator: `Home` and its parts, `build()`, `drawn()` and `problems()`                                                                                           |
| `src/builder/`            | The dashboard builder: a plan's defaults from the home's registries, a person's slots, and the dashboard a plan makes                                                     |
| `demo/`                   | The demo home, Joe's and Jane's, its YAML, and the throwaway instance's entities for it                                                                                   |
| `src/build/`              | `buildBundle()`, and the command line that runs it                                                                                                                        |
| `src/theme/`              | The theme's model, its mapping onto Home Assistant's variables, its contrast claims, its YAML                                                                             |
| `src/test/`               | The jsdom helpers and the fake Home Assistant connection the element tests use                                                                                            |
| `tools/`                  | The throwaway Home Assistant, its look, walk and screenshot passes, the integration's icons, the wiki's pages, and the release zip                                        |
| `custom_components/mnml/` | The integration, and in `www/` (built, git-ignored) everything it serves                                                                                                  |
| `tests/`                  | The integration's tests                                                                                                                                                   |

## `src/contract/`: what the cards and their users both read

| File           | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `entities.ts`  | The id types: `EntityId<Domain>` and one alias per domain (`LightId`, `SensorId`, ...). Also `MdiIcon`, `PopupHash`, `Subnet`, `ServiceName` (a closed union of the services the cards call) and `Corners<T>` (front left, front right, rear left, rear right)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `builder.ts`   | `Plan`, what the panel's builder keeps for a dashboard it made: its title and icon, its rooms by area, its people by `person` entity, its cars by key, its system templates, each with the slots it overrides, how its pop-ups open, and optionally each section's look (`SectionLook`: a title, an icon, and but for System a template; `lookOf()` gives a section's look with the defaults, `SECTION_LOOKS`); `isPlan()`, `isPersonId()`, and `SYSTEM_TEMPLATES`, the templates the builder offers for the System section |
| `cards.ts`     | The configuration of every card: the public interface of MNML; see below                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `defaults.ts`  | `BATTERY_LOW` (20) and `BATTERY_CRITICAL` (5): the tile's problems dot turns orange and red under them. A configuration that writes battery rows reads them too, so the dot and the rows agree                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `subnet.ts`    | `ipv4()` and `subnetRange()`, by which the clients card groups and validates                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `templates.ts` | The template format's types (`Template`, `SlotSpec`, `Rule`, `Kind`, `Value`) with `isTemplate()` and `isMapping()`; see [the template engine](#srctemplates-the-template-engine)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `yaml.ts`      | `toYaml()`, the YAML writer, which quotes YAML 1.1 booleans and sexagesimals so that Home Assistant reads them as strings                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

### The contract, `cards.ts`

- **Cards:** `TileCard`, `EntityCard`, `HeaderCard`, `HeadingCard`, `ListCard` (with `ListRow`), `AgendaCard` (with `AgendaSource`), `MessagesCard`, `ClientsCard` (with `ClientNetwork` and `ClientFields`), `ButtonCard`, `SelectCard`, `SliderCard`, `MediaCard`, `CarPlanCard`, and `PopupsCard` (with `Popup` and `LovelaceCardConfig`, any card a pop-up holds).
- **A tile's or header's subject** is one of two variants: a literal `name` and `icon`, with an optional `entity`; or an `entity` whose name (its device's, with `label`) and icon the card shows, where an `icon` may still override the entity's.
- **`Item`:** an entity with its name, state line, popup and controls. `EntityCard` is an `Item` with a `type` and optional nested `items`: the rows its expander reveals. `TileCard.item` is an `Item` too.
- **Controls:** `toggle`, `slider`, `select`, `service`, `nav`, `indicator`, `status`, `tyres`, `scenes`.
- **`StateItem`:** one entry of a state line. It is one of six variants: an entity's state, an `attribute`, a literal `text`, the `minutes` of a seconds counter, the `serial` number of the entity's device, or the entity's `name`. `icon: true` puts the state icon in front.
- **Rules:** `StateRule` (`is` / `not`); `EntityRule`, which adds the `entity` it reads; and a `status` control's rules, which add the `entities` they watch, how the tooltip names and words them (`label`, `words`), and the `color` they give.
- **`Condition`:** Lovelace's state condition, as `state_not` on an `entity`: the one form a card's `visibility` takes inside a pop-up, which the pop-up shell evaluates.
- **`Problems`:** the leaks and batteries behind a tile's dot.

A card reads nothing the types don't declare, and a key it does not declare is an error (`src/cards/keys.ts`, below). Leave an optional key out to get its default, so the YAML reads as intent: `state` defaults to the entity's own state line on an entity card, and `when` to `{ is: ['on'] }` on a coloured control, pill or header. A list row is the exception: without `when` it is coloured whenever it is shown, so a flag's condition lives in its `show`, and a coloured value row spells its `when`.

A threshold that is a share of something says so in its name. `low_share` and `warn_share` on the `tyres` control, and `tyre_low_share` and `tyre_warn_share` on the car plan, are ratios of a tyre's target (0.9, 0.95). A list row's `low` and `critical` are absolute values in the entity's unit (20, 5 for a battery's percentage).

`cards.ts` is versioned: a new optional key or a new card is a minor release; a renamed or removed key, a changed meaning or a removed card is a major one.

## `src/cards/`: the cards

- `register.ts` is the bundle's entry. It defines sixteen elements, the fourteen cards, the pop-up shell and `mnml-slider` (the slider of the slider card and of a slider control's overlay), and lists the cards and the shell in `window.customCards`. Each card gets its `getStubConfig()` from `stubs.ts`, and each but the pop-ups card its `getConfigElement()` from `edit.ts`. It skips a tag that is already defined, so a second copy of the bundle on one dashboard defines nothing and throws nothing.
- One file per card, named after it in kebab-case; `parts/` holds what several cards share.
- `keys.ts` and `schemas.ts`: every card declares its known keys as a `KeySchema`, built with `schema<T>()` from its interface. `Record<AllKeys<T>, true>` makes the compiler reject a schema that misses a key of the interface or names one it lacks, so the schemas cannot drift from `cards.ts`. A union is checked against the one variant a value picks, `variant<T>()` naming only the keys that variant allows (not those it spells `never`): by its `type` for a control (`tagged()`), and by a marker key for a state item, the select card, a header's or tile's subject and a message source (`marked()`). So a toggle with a `slider`, or a text with an `attribute`, is an unknown key too. `MnmlCard.setConfig()` checks a configuration against its card's schema before anything else, at every depth the schema describes, and allows the layout keys Home Assistant and card-mod add (`grid_options`, `visibility`, `view_layout`, `layout_options`, `card_mod`) at the top.

| Module                                  | Holds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `base.ts`                               | `MnmlCard<C>`, the base class of every card but the pop-up shell and the template card: the key check, configuration, updates only for what the configuration names, holds and teardown, `notify()`, and the default grid size; `Host`, what a part a card draws is given; `requireString()`, `requireNumber()`, `requireList()`, `requireOneOf()` for a card's `validate()`. See [How the cards work](cards.md#lifecycle-of-a-card) |
| `styles.ts`                             | The shared styles, as `css` values: `MOTION_STYLE`, `BASE_STYLE` (its `:host` holds the shared colours as custom properties, `--m-pill`, `--m-hover`, `--m-edge`, `--m-edge-strong`), `HEADING_STYLE`, `ROW_STYLE`, `CONTROL_STYLE`                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `edit.ts`                               | `editorOf(tag)`, each card's `getConfigElement()`: it imports the editors' file by the URL `src/editors/where.ts` gives, and after a failed import asks for it again under a new URL (`?attempt=<n>`), since a browser keeps a failed dynamic import for the page                                                                                                                                                                    |

## `src/templates/`: the template engine

[Templates](templates.md) is the language; this is how it is built.

- `expand.ts`: `expand(templates, instance, discovered, later)` returns `{ card, popups }` and touches nothing else. A name in `later`, a shipped template not loaded yet, is drawn as nothing and listed in `missing`, so one pass names every family a card still needs; a name in neither is an error. It checks each template's slots once (known kinds, lower-case names), resolves each slot (the instance's value, else the discovered one, else the default), checks its kind and its fields, and renders the template's tree: `[[path]]`, `each`/`as`, `if`/`unless`, nested `template:` with `slots:`, keys ending in `?`, lists spliced. A mistake is a `TemplateError` naming the template and the path. `toValue()` copies JSON-like data into a `Value`, so a TypeScript caller converts its interfaces once, without a cast.
- `changes.ts`: `applyChanges(template, changes)` lays the home's changes over a shipped template (set, remove, insert, move, by a path of keys and `#<id>`s) and says which are changed or gone, judged against the shipped template; `isChange()` checks a change's shape for its op; `baseOf()` is the hash a change's `base` holds, of what it touches; `nodeHash()` is the stable hash under it; `changesOf(base, edited)` works out the changes from a shipped template to an edit of it. An `id:` on a list item is a control key to `expand()`, so no card sees it; `ids.test.ts` holds every part of a shipped card or pop-up to one, unique in its list.
- `ids.ts`, `ids.json`, `ids-main.ts`: every released part path, and the retired ones; `pnpm run fix:ids` (part of `pnpm fix`) adds new parts, and `ids.test.ts` fails on one gone without being retired, and on a shipped id that starts with `my-`, the prefix of the ids the panel gives.
- `discover.ts`: `discover(template, area, registries)` fills the slots that have a rule, from the areas, devices, entities and states it is given; with no area, only the `scope: all` rules. It is pure too; the template card hands it `hass`'s registries.
- `shipped.ts`: `readTemplates()` reads `templates/*.yaml` with `yaml`, refusing a name defined twice; `SHIPPED` is what it read, for the generator and the tests. `familyNames()` and `readFamily()` read one file, a family, at a time.
- `families.ts`: the families as the browser gets them: `COMMON`, the shared fragments of `common.yaml`; `OWNER`, the family of every other name; `SHAPES`, the literal card type and `grid_options` of each family template, for sizing a card before its family arrives; and `loadFamily(family)`. In Node it reads the YAML; in the bundle a rolldown plugin in `src/build/bundle.ts` replaces it, with `COMMON`, `OWNER` and `SHAPES` as data and a `loadFamily()` that fetches the family's JSON file next to the bundle, so the browser carries no YAML parser.
- `roles.ts`: `rolesOf(templates)`, each template a tile, a pop-up or a part ([Roles](templates.md#roles)), for the library and the gallery.
- `dashboard.ts`: `expandDashboard(templates, config)` expands every template card of a dashboard and gathers their pop-ups into its popups card, in document order: what a dashboard of templates draws, without a browser.

The template format's types are `src/contract/templates.ts`, part of the public interface beside `cards.ts`.

## `src/home/`: the home generator

A whole dashboard from one typed object: [The home dashboard](home.md) says what it draws.

- `types.ts`: `Home` and its parts (`Room`, `Lights`, `Heating`, `Ac`, `Person`, `Car`, `System` and the rest), every entity spelled with its domain's id type, and the frame (`Dashboard`, `Card`). It is public interface, as the contract is.
- `slots.ts`: one function per subject from its part of the home to its template's slots, in snake_case: `roomSlots()`, `personSlots()`, `proxmoxSlots()`, `systemSlots()`, `headingSlots()` and `snake()`. It computes only what a template cannot: the room's joined, sorted batteries, a person's activities, the server's message sources, the system's firmware per room.
- `view.ts`: `build(home)`, one `sections` view of `custom:mnml-template-card` instances, every slot spelled and no `area`, and the popups card; `drawn(home)`, the same dashboard as the templates expand it, which is what a tool that checks entity ids reads. It expands with the shipped templates only; a home's shared templates are seen by the cards, not by `drawn()`.
- `problems.ts`: `problems(home)`, what would break the dashboard without failing its build: a hash opened that no pop-up defines, a hash defined or producible twice, a key that is no URL fragment, a subnet that is no IPv4 range. A home's tests assert it is empty.

## `src/builder/`: the dashboard builder

What the panel's builder makes a dashboard from. It is pure: it reads the home's registries and the templates it is given, so it runs in the panel and in Node alike.

- `plan.ts`: `planFrom(recipe, registries, templates)` refills a dashboard template in a home: the areas where the rooms section's template draws, every person, the system section's templates whose entities discovery finds, no car, and the sections' looks; `DEFAULT_RECIPE` is the shipped one, and `defaultPlan(registries, templates)`, the quick start, is it refilled: the areas where the room template draws something beyond the area's name and icon, in the order Home Assistant lists them; every `person` entity; each of `SYSTEM_TEMPLATES` whose required slots discovery fills over the whole home; pop-ups that unfold on tablet and desktop.
- `person.ts`: `personOf(registries, entity)`, a person's slots: the key from the entity id, and one device per tracker in the person's `device_trackers` that the companion app (`mobile_app`) made, with the app's sensors on that device by their entity ids' endings (`_battery_level`, `_battery_state`, `_connection_type`, `_ssid`, `_storage`, `_focus`, `_activity`, `_location_permission`). A tracker that lacks one of them is left out, and a person with none is the person entity alone.
- `customized.ts`: from a card its editor changed back to the plan: `roomFrom()` (the area picked, the overrides), `personFrom()` and `systemFrom()` (only what differs from what MNML finds, by `overridesOf()`), and `carFrom()` (the key out of the slots, or no car without one that is a name).
- `recipe.ts`: `recipeOf(plan, templates, shipped)`, a dashboard template from a plan: the sections it has (one with something, or with a look), their looks, the system templates chosen, the openings, and every template it uses, inside others too, that is not the shipped one as shipped, whole; `recipeText()` writes it under `mnml_dashboard:`; `readRecipe(text, shipped)` reads one, refusing a dashboard's configuration, a set of templates, an unknown section, or a section template neither shipped nor bundled, with the reason; `renamedRecipe()` follows the names its templates come in under.
- `dashboard.ts`: `dashboardOf(plan, registries, templates)`, one `sections` view with a heading and the cards of each part that has any (Rooms, People, Garage, System), each heading and template from the section's look, and the popups card. A room is its `area`, discovered live, with its overrides; a person is `personOf()` with the overrides over it; a car is its slots and key. `roomCard()`, `personCard()`, `carCard()` and `systemCard()` make each card alone, for the builder's rows. A system template without overrides is the template alone and discovers live; with them, it holds what discovery found when the plan was built, and the overrides over it, since a card that spells slots does not discover.

## `custom_components/mnml/`: the integration

One config entry (`single_config_entry`), no devices and no entities. Its flow asks nothing.

| File                   | Does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `__init__.py`          | `async_setup_entry()`: the stores, then the websocket commands, the frontend, the panel, the theme and the repairs, the options listener; `async_unload_entry()` takes the bundle and the panel off the pages and clears the repairs; `async_remove_entry()` deletes the theme and gives the default theme back. `MnmlData` (the bundle's URL, whether MNML is the default theme) is the entry's runtime data                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `frontend.py`          | `loader_url(www)`, `/mnml-files/mnml-cards-loader.js?v=<first 8 of the sha256 of the loader and the bundle>`, which fails setup with `ConfigEntryError`, naming what is missing, when the loader, the bundle, the panel or `mnml.yaml` is not built; `async_register_frontend()` serves `www/` at `/mnml-files/` with long cache headers (once per Home Assistant run) and adds the loader to every page with `add_extra_js_url`. The URL comes off the pages on unload, and when a later step of setup fails                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `theme.py`             | `write_theme()` writes `www/mnml.yaml` to `themes/mnml-integration/mnml.yaml`, atomically, when it differs; `async_install_theme()` then reloads themes, and when Home Assistant does not load a theme named MNML from it (no `themes` include, an include of another folder, or `!include_dir_named`, which cannot hold it) takes the folder away again, so the configuration stays valid; `other_theme_files()` finds another file under `themes/` that defines MNML, the standalone theme from HACS in `themes/mnml/` included; `async_apply_default()` sets MNML as the default theme in light and dark mode, or, turned off, gives back each mode MNML still holds (`none`); `async_remove_theme()` deletes the folder and reloads themes, which also gives back a default that named MNML |
| `conflicts.py`         | `async_hand_loaded()`: the URL of a Lovelace resource, stored in the UI or in YAML, that loads `mnml-cards.js` from anywhere but `/mnml-files/`. It reads Lovelace's resource collection, which is not a promised API, and answers nothing when that collection is not what it expects                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `dashboards.py`        | `DashboardStore`: the dashboards the panel's builder made, in `.storage/mnml.dashboards`, by their `url_path`: each one's plan, its last save's time and user, and the version a rebuild replaced (its plan and its Lovelace configuration), which an undo restores. `DASHBOARD_STORE` is its key in `hass.data`, loaded beside the templates' store; one that cannot be read is logged and left out, and its commands answer `not_loaded`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `issues.py`            | The three repairs, raised or cleared on every setup: `theme_not_loaded`, `second_theme`, `hand_loaded_bundle`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `store.py`             | `TemplateStore`: the home's templates in `.storage/mnml.templates`, through Home Assistant's storage helper, each with its last save's time and user and its previous 10 versions; listeners are told after each write. `STORE` is its key in `hass.data`, loaded on the first setup of a run, before the cards are served, so a page that loads them finds the store ready. A store that cannot be read is logged and left out: setup goes on, the websocket answers `not_loaded`, and the cards draw the shipped templates                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `panel.py`             | `async_register_panel()`, the MNML panel at `/mnml` for admins, with the icon `mnml:mnml`, from `www/mnml-cards-panel.js` named by its content; `async_remove_panel()` on unload                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `websocket.py`         | `mnml/templates/subscribe` (every user: the set, then the set again after each save and delete), `save`, `delete` and `history` (admins), and `mnml/dashboards/list`, `save` and `delete` (admins: a plan of the shape of `isPlan()`, and the version it replaces, at a `url_path` of lower case letters and digits with a hyphen between them, as Home Assistant's own dashboards have, at most 512 kB each and 100 in all), registered once per run, with the shape checks of [Templates](templates.md#where-templates-live) and at most 500 templates                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `config_flow.py`       | The flow, and the options form: Use MNML as the default theme                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `translations/en.json` | Every string Home Assistant shows: the flow, the option, the repairs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `brand/`               | The icons, drawn as `icon-light.svg` and `icon-dark.svg`; `pnpm icons` renders each to a PNG of 256 and 512 px with transparent corners: `icon.png` and `icon@2x.png` from the light one, `dark_icon.png` and `dark_icon@2x.png` from the dark one. Home Assistant serves them for the integration, the logo names falling back to the icon of the same theme, and HACS's brand check finds `icon.png`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

**Why a loader.** Home Assistant imports an extra module as soon as its page starts, before its app has installed the scoped custom-element registry it runs on. A card class declared before that extends the browser's own `HTMLElement` and cannot be constructed afterwards. So the page gets `mnml-cards-loader.js` (`src/cards/loader.ts`), which waits until `home-assistant` is defined (`src/cards/started.ts`) and then imports `mnml-cards.js` with its own `?v=`; on a page where Home Assistant already runs it imports at once. Before it waits, the loader registers the `mnml` icon set (`src/cards/iconset.ts`) in `window.customIcons`, as Home Assistant's frontend reads it: `mnml:mnml` is the logo's frame made square, with M and N on the first row and M and the corner on the second, one 24 px path in the colour of wherever it is drawn. Being early, it is there before the sidebar draws the panel's icon.

`/mnml-files/` and not `/mnml/`: the panel takes `/mnml`. `themes/mnml-integration/` and not `themes/mnml/`: HACS installs the standalone MNML Theme there. An update of the integration takes effect after a restart, as for any integration; a reload of the entry serves a rebuilt `www/` under a new `?v=`.

## `demo/`: the demo

- `home.ts`: `DEMO`, a home of nine rooms, Joe and Jane, two cars and the five systems, which draws every template. The demo integration supplies its climates, media players, calendars, camera, vacuum, weather, lock and the kitchen's lights, under their own ids.
- `main.ts` writes `out/demo.yaml`; `tools/dashboard.ts` saves the same dashboard as `mnml-demo` on the throwaway instance.
- `traits.ts`: each demo entity's name, icon (by state where it changes), unit, device class and reading, taken once from the home the demo was made from, with the same names and words scrubbed as in `home.ts`.
- `states.ts`: what makes the demo lived in: the rooms whose lights are off, the rooms heating, who is away, and a few states set outright (an open window, a low and a critical battery, an unlocked car, a stopped guest, a print running).
- `entities.ts`: `packageOf(home)`, a Home Assistant package of template entities, scenes, scripts, helpers and generic thermostats for every id the home draws that the demo integration does not supply, from the traits and the states, and a `customize` block that names and icons the demo integration's entities, the scenes and the thermostats (`customizeOf()`), which `tools/demo.ts` also writes to the registry of those that have an entry, since a card reads a registered entity's name from the registry; run, it writes `.ha/packages/demo.yaml` and copies the QR, map and 3D printer images to `.ha/www/`. `created()` lists the ids a package makes, and its test holds the two together. `tools/demo.ts` adds the people and their device trackers, home or away, the 3D printer's camera from its image, and to each numeric template sensor a display precision of as many decimals as its reading, renames what Home Assistant kept from an earlier run, removes the demo's entities the package does not make, and fails on an id another integration took first, which belongs in `SUPPLIED`.

## `src/build/`: the build

- `buildBundle(file)` is one rolldown build for the browser, of minified ES modules written beside `file`. Three entries keep fixed names: `mnml-cards.js`, the bundle (`src/cards/register.ts`); `mnml-cards-loader.js` (`src/cards/loader.ts`); and `mnml-cards-panel.js` (`src/panel/main.ts`), which the integration registers, and whose `yaml` package reaches no dashboard.
- **The card editors** (`src/editors/main.ts`) are a chunk of their own, `mnml-cards-editors-<hash>.js`, which nothing imports statically. The build fills the generated module `src/editors/where.ts` with its URL, and a card imports it from its `getConfigElement()` (`src/cards/edit.ts`). The URL is a module of its own on purpose: a browser keeps a failed dynamic import for the page, so a retry asks for the same file under a fresh URL, `?attempt=<n>`. The editors carry no YAML parser, since Home Assistant's own YAML tab covers YAML.
- **Shared chunks.** What several entries share is a chunk named by its content, `mnml-cards-<name>-<hash>.js`.
- **The literals are minified.** A plugin runs `minify-literals` (lightningcss for the styles, html-minifier-next for the markup) over every file under `src/` that holds a `css`, `html` or `svg` template.
- **The families.** `common.yaml` goes in as data. Every other family is written beside the bundle as `mnml-cards-<family>.json`, and the bundle names each by its content (`?v=<hash>`), since the integration serves them with long cache headers.
- **A build starts clean.** It first removes every file of the folder whose name starts with the bundle's stem (`mnml-cards`), so no chunk of an earlier build stays beside the new ones.
- **Each map is named by its content.** Every file has its source map beside it, sources included, so a browser's developer tools show the TypeScript and a stack trace names it. The file's last line is `//# sourceMappingURL=<file>.map?v=<hash>`, the map's own hash. The files are served with long cache headers, so a fixed name could pair a new file with an older map; a new map is a new URL. Its paths are relative to this repository (`src/...`).
- `node src/build/main.ts [out]` writes them into `out` (resolved from the working directory), the bundle under the name `src/build/names.ts` gives; `pnpm run build:frontend` gives it `custom_components/mnml/www/`, and a project that holds MNML as a submodule builds into its own folder.
- `node src/theme/main.ts [out]` writes `mnml.yaml` there, after every contrast claim holds; `pnpm run build:theme` gives it the same folder. `pnpm build` runs both.

## Releases

`.github/workflows/check.yml` runs on every pull request and every push to `main`, as jobs that run side by side, each on its own runner: `lint` (oxfmt, oxlint, markdownlint, knip), `typescript` (vitest), `python` (ruff, ruff format, mypy), `pytest`, `hassfest`, `floor` (the Python tests on the oldest Home Assistant supported) and `hacs` (HACS's validation). Together they run every step of `pnpm check`, and `build.test.ts` fails when a step of it is in no job. A tag `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`, one release at a time: the same checks, by calling `check.yml`, and beside them the build job, a check that the tag is `v` and the version in `manifest.json`, `pnpm build` and `pnpm zip`; once both pass, a GitHub release with `mnml.zip` attached and generated notes. `hacs.json` sets `zip_release`, so HACS unpacks `mnml.zip` into `custom_components/mnml/`; a hand install does the same.

HACS's validation runs every check, its brand check satisfied by `brand/icon.png`; hassfest checks the manifest and `build.test.ts` holds `hacs.json`. Every action is pinned to a commit, so a moved tag cannot change what CI runs; the build job reads the repository only, without credentials left on disk, and only the publish job, which runs no repository code, may write. A tag with a `-` (`v0.2.0-rc.1`) makes a prerelease, which HACS offers only to those who ask for it. The publishing step skips a release that already exists, so a release that failed half way is re-run as it is.

Dependabot (`.github/dependabot.yml`) opens a pull request each week for the Python tools (uv), the Node packages (pnpm) and the pinned actions; `pytest-homeassistant-custom-component` and `home-assistant-frontend` move together in one. Its security updates bump only the vulnerable package itself, so a package Home Assistant pins exactly, such as PyJWT or cryptography, is fixed by the weekly bump of `pytest-homeassistant-custom-component`, which brings the Home Assistant that pins a patched version. Those packages serve the tests only; the integration requires none. `.github/workflows/dependabot.yml` turns on auto-merge for Dependabot's patch and minor updates, so they squash into `main` once the checks pass. It names the two kinds it merges rather than the one it skips, so an update whose kind it cannot read waits too, as a major one does; and it acts only when Dependabot both opened the pull request and pushed to it.

## The repository

- **`main` takes changes only through pull requests.** A ruleset requires a pull request whose checks, the jobs of `check.yml`, pass, merges it by squashing, keeps the history linear, and refuses a force-push or a deletion of `main`. A merged branch is deleted.
- **Release tags stay put.** A second ruleset refuses to move or delete a `v*` tag, so a release always names the commit CI built.
- **The wiki is made from `docs/`.** `.github/workflows/wiki.yml` runs `tools/wiki.ts` on every push to `main` that changes `README.md` or `docs/`, and pushes the result to the wiki: each doc becomes a page named after its title and the README the Home page; a link between docs becomes a link between pages, and a link to any other file an absolute link to GitHub; a sidebar lists the pages, and each page names the file it is made from. The docs stay the source, written and reviewed with the code; the wiki is for reading.
- **Reports.** `SECURITY.md` sends a vulnerability to GitHub's private advisories. An issue opens from a bug or a feature form (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`), and a pull request from a checklist (`.github/pull_request_template.md`).

## Tests

- **The integration's tests** are in `tests/`, on `pytest-homeassistant-custom-component`, which runs a real Home Assistant in each test, with `home-assistant-frontend` for the frontend it depends on. The fixtures in `conftest.py` give each test a `www/` of its own (`const.WWW` is patched), a config folder with the themes include, `setup_mnml()` and `themes()` (the frontend's `frontend/get_themes`). `pnpm test` runs them, after vitest, on the current Home Assistant (2026.10.0b2); `pnpm run test:python-floor` on the oldest supported (2026.10.0b0, the first with probatio, the validation library that replaces voluptuous), with its own harness and frontend.
- **The TypeScript tests**, `*.test.ts`, sit next to what they cover and run on vitest, in the two projects of `vitest.config.ts`: `node`, for the contract, the engine, the generator, the builder, the theme, the build, the tools and the demo; and `browser`, on jsdom, for the cards, `src/ha/`, the store, the editors, the panel and `src/test/`. `test` comes from vitest, assertions from `node:assert/strict`. vitest runs each file in a module state of its own, so a test that needs an empty store or registry is a file of its own; `template-failure.test.ts` and `template-card-failure.test.ts` replace `families.ts` with `vi.mock()`, so a card and the template card's gallery meet a family that cannot be loaded.
- **Elements are mounted** with `src/test/render.ts`: `define()` defines a tag once, `mounted()` puts an element in the document and waits for its update, then gives its shadow root, `text()` reads the text a user sees, and `drawn()` renders a template into a box of its own. A test queries the shadow root and sends real DOM events.
- `src/test/fake-hass.ts` is a fake connection for the store: `fakeStore()` answers `mnml/templates/subscribe` with `kept` (or as a home without the integration when it is unset), refuses with `refuse`, sends a save with `keep()`, records each message and each subscription's options, and reconnects.
- `styles.test.ts` asserts that every `--mnml-*` variable a card reads has a fallback, so the cards work under any theme.
- `editors/cards.test.ts` and `editors/form.test.ts` send every card the demo draws, and every example card, through its editor's description and through Home Assistant's form data, section by section and part by part, and want each back unchanged, key order included; the type checker holds each description to every key of its contract type.
- `src/cards/templates.test.ts` expands every shipped template from its `example`, and again with only its required slots, and gives each MNML card it draws, at any depth, to that card's `setConfig()`: a key a card does not know fails wherever an example reaches it, and a branch no example fills goes unchecked. It also holds every object slot to its declared `fields:`, and every path into one to a declared field. `src/templates/docs.test.ts` fails when `docs/templates.md` misses a template, a slot or a field.
- `examples/cards.yaml` is a hand-written configuration of every card, on the `demo` integration's entities and the template entities of `examples/fixtures.yaml`. `tools/` installs it on a throwaway Home Assistant and looks at it under both themes. `examples/templates.yaml` is a second view, rooms placed by `area`, which `tools/areas.ts` fills by moving demo entities into two areas.

### The throwaway Home Assistant

It runs in Docker, from `.ha/` (git-ignored), with `custom_components/mnml/` of this tree mounted read-only, and has no tie to a home. Then:

```bash
pnpm demo
```

`tools/up.ts` does the whole round, and runs again as often as wanted:

1. writes `.ha/configuration.yaml` the first time (the `demo` integration, the themes folder, the packages), and copies `recipes/messages.yaml` and `examples/fixtures.yaml` into `.ha/packages/`;
2. writes the demo's package with `node demo/entities.ts`, and builds `custom_components/mnml/www/` (`pnpm build`);
3. starts `ghcr.io/home-assistant/home-assistant:beta` afresh (the beta channel, while the oldest Home Assistant supported is a beta) as the container `mnml-ha`, published on `127.0.0.1:8124` only, and waits until Home Assistant answers;
4. on a `.ha/` with no owner yet, onboards it: the owner `demo`, password `demo`, and a long-lived token written to `.env` (git-ignored) with `HA_URL=http://localhost:8124`; then waits until Home Assistant is running;
5. runs `tools/demo.ts` (the demo's people, device trackers, camera, names, icons and display precisions), `tools/areas.ts` (the two areas the examples' templates view places rooms in), `tools/ids.ts` (every id in the examples and the demo exists), and `tools/dashboard.ts`, which removes what an older install put in `.ha/` (the `/local/mnml` resources, `www/mnml-cards*`, `themes/mnml.yaml`), adds the MNML entry or reloads it, saves the templates of `examples/home-templates.yaml` to the store, removes the `mnml-templates` dashboard an older install made, saves the `mnml-examples` and `mnml-demo` dashboards, and reloads the themes.

The tools reach it over Home Assistant's websocket through `home-assistant-js-websocket` (`tools/socket.ts`), and refuse an `HA_URL` that is not local (`tools/env.ts`), so one run from another project's folder cannot reach a home with that project's token. `docker stop mnml-ha` stops it; deleting `.ha/` and `.env` starts over. Then, by hand, each in Playwright's Chromium (`tools/browser.ts`, installed once with `pnpm exec playwright install chromium`), signed in with the token:

```bash
pnpm look           # out/look/: the default theme and MNML, light and dark, phone and desktop
pnpm walk           # the panel, walked through: edit, save, reset, new, duplicate, delete, build a dashboard
pnpm screenshots    # docs/screenshots/: the demo for the README, light and dark, six pop-ups and the panel; then tools/split.ts joins the desktop's light and dark diagonally into desktop.png
```

`pnpm look` fails on any error card on the examples' cards and templates views, on a card of the examples whose editor cannot be opened or opens without a form (it mounts each inside `home-assistant`, whose context Home Assistant's pickers read), on a panel that lists no template or a shipped template whose builder does not open or shows a problem, and on a demo pop-up that opens nothing, has no header or shows a blank body. The panel and the demo it checks under MNML, light and dark, opening each of the demo's 46 pop-ups by its hash. The screenshots are read by eye: under the default theme each card keeps its hairline edge and its pills.

`pnpm walk` drives the panel on a desktop: it opens `room`, picks a part, edits a slot's label, sees the slot marked changed and the change counted in the header, saves, and finds `room` customised in the library; resets it to shipped and saves; makes a new template and saves it; duplicates it and sees the copy open under its own name; leaves another new template unsaved and finds its name free again; and deletes the first. Then it forgets every dashboard MNML built, finds the offer to build one, makes one by Quick start and opens it (template cards, no error card), rebuilds it with a new title and a room fewer, undoes the rebuild, and forgets it with Delete it too. It fails on a step that does not hold, and on a page error from MNML's files.

## Tooling

**Oxc for TypeScript, ruff and mypy for Python.**

- `oxlint`, with `typeAware` and `typeCheck` through `oxlint-tsgolint`, lints and reports the TypeScript diagnostics. There is no `tsc` and no `typescript` package.
- `oxfmt` formats; `knip` finds dead code; `rolldown` bundles the elements, and `minify-literals` minifies their templates; `vitest` runs the TypeScript tests, the elements' on jsdom.
- `ruff` lints and formats the Python, `mypy --strict` type checks it, and hassfest, Home Assistant's own validator, checks the integration in Docker (`ghcr.io/home-assistant/hassfest`, `linux/amd64`). HACS's validation reads the GitHub repository, so it runs in CI only.
- There are no git hooks. The bundle's one runtime dependency is Lit, which the build bundles; the integration has none; `home-assistant-js-websocket` is the tools' client for the throwaway Home Assistant.

| Tool         | Configuration                           | Rules of the house                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| oxlint       | `oxlint.config.ts`                      | Every rule is an error (`denyWarnings`), and so is an unused disable directive. A rule that fights a convention is turned off in the config, with the reason written here, never in an inline directive. `no-console` and `no-await-in-loop` are off for `src/*/main.ts`, `demo/main.ts`, `demo/entities.ts` and `tools/*.ts`, the command lines, which print and run one step after another on purpose. `no-console` is off for `src/cards/parts/popup-registry.ts`, which reports a hash announced twice on the console, where a dashboard's author looks, for `src/store/store.ts`, which reports there a card that threw on a change of the store and changes kept in a shape it does not know, for `src/store/shipped.ts`, which reports a family that could not be loaded, and for their tests, `template-failure.test.ts` and `template-card-failure.test.ts`, which replace `console.error` to see those reports or keep them quiet |
| oxfmt        | `oxfmt.config.ts`                       | The defaults (100 columns, semicolons, trailing commas, sorted `package.json`) plus single quotes and sorted imports                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| markdownlint | `.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc`              | Every rule but MD013, line length: a paragraph is one line. `CLAUDE.md`, an `@AGENTS.md` include, is skipped, and so is `.github/pull_request_template.md`, which starts a pull request's description and so opens with a second-level heading                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| vitest       | `vitest.config.ts`                      | Two projects: `node`, and `browser` on jsdom, each with the folders its tests run in ([Tests](#tests)). `test` comes from vitest, assertions from `node:assert/strict`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| knip         | `knip.jsonc`                            | Fails on unused files, dependencies and exports. Don't export what only the same file uses. Entries: the four the browser loads (`src/cards/register.ts`, `src/cards/loader.ts`, `src/editors/main.ts`, `src/panel/main.ts`), the contract (`cards.ts`, `entities.ts`, `templates.ts`) and the home's types (`src/home/types.ts`), whose exports are for the projects that use MNML, the tests, `tools/*.ts` and `demo/*.ts`. `uv` is a binary it leaves alone                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ruff         | `pyproject.toml`                        | Every rule but `D` (the code has no comments, so no docstrings), `COM812` (it fights ruff's formatter) and `CPY001` (no copyright headers); in `tests/` also `S101` (pytest asserts), `PLR2004` (expected values are literals), `SLF001` and `ARG001` (fixtures, and Home Assistant's test internals). 100 columns, Python 3.13 syntax                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| mypy         | `pyproject.toml`                        | `strict`, over `custom_components/` and `tests/`, with `explicit_package_bases` since `custom_components/` has no `__init__.py`. Two overrides: `pytest_homeassistant_custom_component` ships no types, and `homeassistant.components.http` re-exports `StaticPathConfig`, which the oldest Home Assistant supported defines there itself                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| hassfest     | `manifest.json`, `translations/en.json` | Home Assistant's rules for an integration: the manifest's keys, the config flow, the translations                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| tsconfig     | `tsconfig.json`                         | `src/`, `demo/`, `tools/` and `vitest.config.ts`. Strict, with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` but without `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`: an optional key may hold `undefined`, which a card reads as absent. `experimentalDecorators` and `useDefineForClassFields: false` are Lit's decorators as Home Assistant writes them: a class field defined by the standard would shadow the accessor a decorator puts on the class. rolldown and vitest compile them; Node, which only strips types, runs no module that imports an element                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

- **Markdown too.** oxfmt formats the docs and realigns a table's columns to their display width. Leave a table to `pnpm fix` rather than padding it by hand.
- **Ignored paths.** `ignorePatterns` keeps oxfmt off `uv.lock`, `.ha/`, `out/`, `.venv/` and `custom_components/mnml/www/`. All the tools honour `.gitignore`.
- **Dependencies.** `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `uv.lock` hold the exact versions; `pnpm install` and `uv sync` install them, and CI's `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `uv sync --locked` refuse a lock that has drifted. `packageManager` in `package.json` names the pnpm. pnpm runs a dependency's install script only when the project allows it, and this one allows none, so no dependency may rely on one.
